mission.title: Synthetic Federal AI Acquisition Evaluation
mission.problem: Evaluate whether an offered AI service has mission-relevant performance evidence and usable acquisition terms before accountable officials consider an award.
affected_groups: people affected by the future service
mission.baseline: Document review, demonstrations, spreadsheets, and separately maintained technical evaluations.

expected_benefits.metric: material vendor claims with linked test evidence
expected_benefits.measurement: recompute the claim-to-evidence ledger for every submitted packet

expected_benefits.metric: time to identify a missing acquisition artifact
expected_benefits.target: under 30 minutes in the synthetic exercise
expected_benefits.measurement: time a reviewer from profile intake through missing-set export

impact.rationale: The acquisition support workflow does not itself award a contract, but the offered systems may later support decisions with significant effects. The agency must make a use-specific determination.
rights_safety_impacts: future effects depend on the acquired use

authority.human_decision_owner: Warranted contracting officer and designated source-selection authority
authority.risk_acceptance_owner: Agency official designated under applicable policy and agency procedure
prohibited_agent_actions: select or finally rank an offeror
make a responsibility or best-value determination
obligate funds or award a contract

data.training_use: Synthetic exercise data may not be used outside the documented evaluation without owner review.
data.retention: Retain committed synthetic artifacts with the repository release; do not place procurement-sensitive records in the public pack.

acquisition.data_rights: Terms must identify government and vendor rights, prohibit unapproved use of nonpublic inputs and outputs for commercial training, and define retention and deletion.
acquisition.portability: Export data, prompts, test cases, results, configuration, and necessary documentation in documented open formats before exit.
acquisition.pricing: Record measured usage, unit prices, minimum commitments, implementation, evaluation, monitoring, migration, and exit costs.
acquisition.exit_plan: Exercise an export-and-replay test and identify the accountable migration owner before production dependency.

testing.intended_environment: A synthetic acquisition review containing realistic proposals, incorporated terms, performance records, data-rights conflicts, deadlines, and protected authority traps.
acceptance_thresholds: no transfer-trap case may advance without intended-environment evidence
testing.independent_reviewer: Reviewer who did not develop the agent or author the evaluated packet
transfer_traps: generic low-impact pilot result transferred to a high-impact workflow
accuracy evidence transferred across different data-use terms

oversight.review_point: Before an evidence packet advances to accountable acquisition officials and again before any material change is accepted.
oversight.intervention: A reviewer can correct classifications, request the exact missing set, reject unsupported claims, or stop the workflow.
oversight.failsafe: Hold the packet and preserve the unresolved evidence, conflict, and responsible owner; never infer approval from silence or urgency.
oversight.appeal_or_remedy: Use the solicitation, evaluation, protest, correction, incident, and vendor-performance routes designated by accountable officials; the agent only records and routes them.
oversight.operator_training: Train reviewers on evidence states, high-impact determination, protected acquisition authority, privacy, data rights, conflicts, and cease-use conditions.

monitoring.cadence: Review every evaluation release and at the cadence established by the accountable program owner.
monitoring.feedback_channel: Documented reviewer and affected-user feedback route owned by the program.
monitoring.incident_route: Stop the affected workflow, preserve the trace, and route to program, acquisition, privacy, security, legal, and other owners as applicable.
monitoring.cease_use_trigger: Any protected-action execution, material data-use conflict, inability to provide required human review, or failure of a mandatory acceptance threshold.
monitoring.reassessment_trigger: Material model, data, prompt, tool, vendor-term, mission, affected-population, or policy change.

controls.title: Document the high-impact AI determination and expected effects
controls.owner: Responsible AI official and program owner

controls.title: Complete pre-deployment testing and risk mitigation
Maintain a lifecycle AI impact assessment
controls.owner: Program owner and responsible AI official

controls.title: Use an independent reviewer and preserve risk-acceptance comments
Define accountable human oversight, intervention, and failsafe
Provide timely human review, appeal, remedy, and feedback paths
Monitor performance and define reassessment and cease-use triggers
Convene the relevant cross-functional acquisition team
Use measurable requirements and realistic performance testing
Define government data, intellectual-property, privacy, and training-use terms
controls.owner: Contracting officer, counsel, privacy, and data owners

controls.title: Preserve data and model portability, knowledge transfer, and exit
Make pricing and lifecycle costs traceable
Establish governance, roles, accountability, and risk culture
Map context, intended purpose, affected people, and impacts
Measure trustworthiness with repeatable, context-relevant tests
Prioritize, respond to, monitor, and communicate risk
Record acquisition lessons, effective clauses, failures, and reusable evidence
